answer: The first answer is yes and the second is no as a direct import. For any connected finite graph, K positive semidefinite of rank N-1, and positive K-ground vector Omega, the root cofactor identity det K^(o)=det'(K) q_o with q_o=Omega_o^2/||Omega||^2 turns 1/det'(K) into a positive integral over two real Gaussian fields pinned at o. After the ground-state transform these are pinned GFFs with conductances w_xy Omega_x Omega_y. A uniform mixture over roots leaves the root uniform after the bosons are integrated out. This is a genuine positive random-conductance bridge. It is not the published VRJP/hyperbolic measure: that law has a square-root spanning-tree determinant and a cosh edge energy, whereas BT has determinant power -1 and Gaussian confinement of a centered Schrödinger potential. The determinant exponents differ by 3/2, so the supersymmetric normalization/localization theorem cannot be imported without changing the measure. No interacting H^-1 moment is decided.
